newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tax talk kicks off first ECOFIN of 97.
newsitem.headline: Tax talk kicks off first ECOFIN of 97.

text.p: European Union finance ministers began the first ECOFIN Council of the year on Monday, focusing on calls to bring Europe's diverse tax systems into line and aiming to avoid any controversy concerning the single currency.

During a publicly broadcast roundtable discussion kicking off Monday's meeting, most finance minsters focused on the need to harmonise EU tax laws in order to prevent unfair competition among countries in the single market.
"This is a subject which has been neglected far too long," Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi said.
With few substantial issues on the agenda, the ministers were expected to hold informal discussions on next month's Group of Seven meeting in Berlin.
They were also to meet their counterparts from central and eastern Europe countries later in the day.
EU sources said there was likely to be an informal discussion on France's proposal for a G7-like council to discuss economic policy under a common currency.

Although the proposal has come under fire from the Bundesbank, which fears it might be used to undermine the independence of the future European Central Bank (ECB), few countries expect a major row at this stage.

"I do not understand the reaction from several people (to the proposal)," Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said as he arrived for the meeting. "There is no reason at all for becoming nervous."
Juncker is also Luxembourg's finance minsister and will chair EU finance ministers' meetings during the Grand Duchy's EU presidency in the second six months of this year,
